newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open down 1.00 to 2.00 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open down 1.00 to 2.00 cents.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 to 2.00 cents lower Friday in a technical correction to Thursday's sharp run-up, traders said.
But traders remained cautious, noting the market's habit of ignoring pre-opening expectations.
"It's been called down all week and hasn't made it," said one trader. "It'll probably be closer to unchanged. Technically, it's probably overbought and vunerable to a big sell-off."

Thursday, New York arabica futures ended sharply higher, bolstered by speculative buying and keen interest in the nearby spreads. September jumped 8.25 cents, to 208.80 cents, after ranging between 209.75 and 199.50 cents. December rose 6.00 cents, to 176.25 cents, while the back months closed 1.00 to 3.95 cents higher.
The September/December switch widened to 32.55 cents compared with 30.30 cents at the close on Wednesday, while December/March 1998 stretched to 21.25 cents versus 19.20 cents.
Technically, September resistance was pegged at 210.00 cents, while support was seen at 206.00 cents, traders said.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Friday that cooler weather is forecast over the weekend into next week in Brazil's coffee belt, however, no damaging cold weather is expected. Temperatures will be near to below normal, WSC said.
After Thursday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 1,530 60-kg bags as of August 6, to 90,929 bags. An additional 3,218 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

London robusta futures were mixed early Friday, with the nearby contracts sinking. At the midday break, September was down $14, at the low of $1,630, after peaking at $1,650. November fell $6, to $1,640.
